source_meta.fetched_note: Official Telangana State Waqf Board properties page. Contains two tables: (1) 'Indicative statement showing particulars of encroachment on Waqf institutions and attached properties in Telangana' — institutions, total area (acres), encroached area (acres) per district, with a state total row; (2) 'List of institutions in Telangana region category wise as per 1st survey' — category breakdown (Dargah, Graveyard, Mosque, Ashoorkhana, Chilla, Takia, Others) per district. Both tables use the 10 pre-2016 undivided ('old') Telangana districts, not the ~33 post-2016/2019 reorganised districts. Page explicitly states: 'Separation of data according to the new districts re organisation work is in progress' and carries the disclaimer: 'The published data is only informative, correctness of data should be re-verified by WAQF board without any legal binding.'

Board history: predecessor 'Umoor-E-Mazhabi' body under the Nizam; Muslim Waqf Board established by notification No. 90 dated 13-01-1955 (Hyderabad Gazette), effective 15-01-1955; reconstituted as AP State Waqf Board in July 1996 under the Wakf Act 1995 (in force from 1-1-1996), later becoming Telangana State Waqf Board post state bifurcation. Cites same overall figures as the properties page: 32,157-33,929 institutions (figures vary by section) and 77,538 acres total, with 'more than 55,000 acres out of 77,000 encroached.' No explicit mention found of a 1960s/70s survey or its 1989 publication, or of the 2,186 missing-records High Court matter, within the fetched content.

News analysis confirming state totals (33,929 institutions; 77,538.07 acres total; 57,423.91 acres [~75%] encroached; estimated value of encroached land ~Rs 4 lakh crore) and confirming the Waqf Board admitted to the Telangana High Court that records for 2,186 Waqf properties were missing (no case name/date given in article). Corroborates category totals: 1,869 dargahs, 8,521 graveyards, 3,052 mosques, 11,056 ashurkhanas, 6,789 chillas, 112 takias, 2,530 others.

They do NOT yet reflect the ~33 post-reorganisation districts. A separately reported 2025 UMEED-portal-transition figure of 'around 85,000 properties' and '~20,000 mutawallis' across '77,000+ acres' (source: newsonair.gov.in, Oct 2025, quoting Waqf Board chairman Azmatullah Hussaini) could not be reconciled to a district level and is not merged into this total — flagged as a data gap.

board_context.history: Waqf affairs in the Hyderabad State were administered as 'Umoor-E-Mazhabi' under the Nizam's rule. A dedicated Muslim Waqf Board was established by the Raj Pramukh via Notification No. 90 dated 13-01-1955 (published in the Hyderabad Gazette), effective 15-01-1955, under the Wakf Act 1954. Following the Wakf Act 1995 (in force 1-1-1996), the Andhra Pradesh State Waqf Board was reconstituted in July 1996; AP was noted as the first state in India to frame election rules and conduct elections for waqf board representation under that Act. After the 2014 bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, the Telangana State Waqf Board came into being for the Telangana region, headquartered in Hyderabad, functioning under the Telangana Ministry of Minority Affairs. Current chairman referenced in 2025 sources: Azmatullah Hussaini (an earlier/different source names Mohammed Masiullah Khan as chairman; leadership may have changed between sources).
board_context.survey_years: The official district/category table is explicitly labelled 'as per 1st survey' but the exact survey year was not stated verbatim on the properties page itself. Corroborating court record (P. Srinivas vs State of Telangana, 10-03-2020, Indian Kanoon) references a Waqf gazette notification dated 09-02-1989 publicly declaring specific parcels (e.g., Boduppal village, Ac. 294.20 guntas) as waqf property — consistent with, but not definitive confirmation of, a survey conducted in the 1960s/70s and gazetted around 1989 as referenced in secondary literature. No evidence was found in these sources of any newer, completed state-wide re-survey; the 2025 shift to the UMEED portal (replacing the now-disabled WAMSI system as of 8 May 2025) appears to be the current mechanism for updating property records, and Telangana was still in early data-upload/training stages as of October 2025.
board_context.known_data_gaps: 1) Telangana Waqf Board admitted to the Telangana High Court that records for 2,186 Waqf properties (which were encroached) were missing, reportedly worsened by the 2014 AP bifurcation. 2) The official properties page itself states district data has not been re-mapped to the ~33 post-2016/2019 reorganised districts ('Separation of data according to the new districts re organisation work is in progress'), so all figures in this file use the 10 old/undivided districts only. 3) A 2025 figure of ~85,000 properties / ~20,000 mutawallis (UMEED portal transition, per Oct 2025 news) is roughly 2.5x the 33,929-institution 1st-survey count and has no public district-level breakdown, so it is not merged into district-level figures here. 4) No mandal-level or GIS/geocoded data was found in any public official source as of this research.

litigation_cases.case_name: The Telangana State Waqf Board vs M/S. Solithro Private Limited
litigation_cases.citation: Writ Appeal No. 1432 of 2016 (with W.P. No. 23242 of 2008)
litigation_cases.property_involved: Lands notified as Waqf in Survey Nos. 136, 137, 227 and 228, Shabhaspally village, and land in Sikindlapur Village, Shivampet Mandal
litigation_cases.location: Narsapur and Siddipet Taluks, Medak District, Telangana
litigation_cases.dispute_summary: Telangana State Waqf Board appealed a single judge order that quashed a 2001 notification declaring these lands as Waqf property, after Solithro Private Limited purchased the land at a bank auction in 2013-14. The company argued the 2001 notification was issued under the repealed 1954 Wakf Act and was therefore void.
litigation_cases.outcome_status: Court sided with the purchaser; the 2001 Waqf notification was quashed as void (issued under repealed law), and revenue authorities were directed to decide ownership afresh, effectively de-notifying the land as Waqf.

litigation_cases.outcome_status: Appeal partly allowed: claimants held entitled to compensation for Sy. No. 407/5 since the Board failed to prove dedication predated the 1941 purchase; Sy. No. 400/A matter remitted for further proceedings.

litigation_cases.case_name: Telangana State Waqf Board vs Mohamed Muzafar
litigation_cases.property_involved: Graveyard 'Mir Rahmat Ali Shah' (Muntakhab No. 998) including an occupied tenancy portion and an encroached portion
litigation_cases.area: 998.66 sq. yards total; Schedule A 90.16 sq. yards, Schedule B (encroached) 40 sq. yards
litigation_cases.dispute_summary: Waqf Board alleged the respondent was an unlawful occupant — a defaulting tenant on part of the graveyard land and an encroacher on another part — while the respondent disputed the Waqf status and the gazette notification's expanded area.
litigation_cases.outcome_status: Supreme Court upheld the Waqf Tribunal's finding that the properties were legitimate Waqf property; respondent given three months to vacate and pay rent arrears.

litigation_cases.case_name: Mohammed Azeem Khan vs Telangana State Waqf Board
litigation_cases.property_involved: Dargah Hazrat Syed Saadullah Hussaini, Badapahad - offerings/tender rights
litigation_cases.dispute_summary: Dispute over award of a sealed tender for collection of offerings at the Dargah after the highest bidder deposited funds one day after the stipulated deadline; the second-highest bidder challenged the award as improper.
litigation_cases.outcome_status: Petition dismissed; court held the deposit was timely given intervening bank holidays, and the tender award to the highest bidder stood.

litigation_cases.case_name: Telangana State Waqf Board vs The State Of Telangana
litigation_cases.property_involved: Property No. 3-3-844, notified as Waqf under A.P. Gazette dated 12.07.1984, occupied by long-term tenants
litigation_cases.dispute_summary: Waqf Board challenged a 2002 Lok Adalat award that had settled a specific performance suit for sale of the property between private parties, arguing the sale agreement was void because the land was Waqf property and the seller had no authority to alienate it.
litigation_cases.outcome_status: Writ petition dismissed on grounds of 21-year delay/laches in challenging the award despite the Board's knowledge since 2002.

litigation_cases.case_name: Syed Raza Aman And 5 Others vs The Telangana State Waqf Board And 9 Others
litigation_cases.property_involved: Ibadat Khana-e-Hussaini (IKH), a Waqf religious institution established via Waqf Deed dated 30 February 1953 (Municipal Nos. 22-2-638 to 643)
litigation_cases.dispute_summary: Internal dispute between two Shia sects (Akhbari and Usuli) over control of the prayer facility and the Managing Committee's authority to require an application form for religious functions such as Majlis-e-Aza.
litigation_cases.outcome_status: High Court partly reversed the Tribunal's injunction, allowing the Managing Committee to continue requiring the application form while upholding a restriction on removing photographs.

litigation_cases.case_name: Mushke Srinivas Reddy vs The Telangana State Waqf Board
litigation_cases.property_involved: Property in Survey No. 15, House No. 3-9, declared Waqf via a 1990 Gazette Notification
litigation_cases.location: Gudur Village, Bibinagar Mandal, Nalgonda District
litigation_cases.dispute_summary: Purchasers holding 2013 sale deeds discovered the property had been notified as Waqf land in 1990 and challenged the notification's validity, alleging procedural defects and lack of notice to prior owners, amid pending eviction proceedings by the Board.
litigation_cases.outcome_status: Court modified the lower order, granting the purchasers liberty to pursue an alternative remedy/forum for the factual dispute rather than compelling them into the pending eviction proceedings; no opinion expressed on merits.

litigation_cases.case_name: Syeda Kaneezesakina Moosavi vs Telangana State Waqf Board & Others
litigation_cases.property_involved: Bargah-e-Hazrath-e-Abbas (AS) Waqf institution, including a 'Ladies Room' occupied for 55 years
litigation_cases.area: Institution spans 1,344 square yards; Ladies Room 120 square feet
litigation_cases.dispute_summary: Dispute over appointment of Mutawalli (trustee) to a roughly 450-year-old Waqf institution, involving hereditary succession rights from a 1983 judgment, whether a female heir could hold the post, and the petitioner's alleged unlawful eviction from a residential room within the institution.
litigation_cases.outcome_status: High Court dismissed revision petitions, upholding the Tribunal's order for Mutawalli appointment under the correct statutory provision with a one-year tenure, respecting 1983 hereditary succession guidelines.

litigation_cases.case_name: M. Govinda Rao And Ors. vs A.P. State Wakf Board And Ors.
litigation_cases.property_involved: Qazi Service Inam Wakf lands, Survey Nos. 201-203/2
litigation_cases.location: Nidamanuru Village, Krishna District, Andhra Pradesh
litigation_cases.dispute_summary: Challenge to a government order permitting sale of Wakf land to tenant-occupants at Rs. 6 lakh/acre, far below an estimated market value of Rs. 30-40 lakh/acre, bypassing the Wakf Act's mandatory public auction requirement.
litigation_cases.outcome_status: Court declared the government order illegal for bypassing Section 51's mandatory public auction requirement, upheld cancellation of the sale, and directed refund with interest to the buyers.

litigation_cases.case_name: Shaik Madhar Saheb vs The State Of Telangana
litigation_cases.property_involved: Wakf land endowed for a Muslim Maternity Hospital, Survey Nos. 231, 242, 252, 256, 258-269, 280, 281, 450, 451, 457-459, 463, 469, 486, 487, 581
litigation_cases.area: Approximately 428 acres (12-16 acres allegedly sold without authorization), valued over Rs. 1000 crores
litigation_cases.dispute_summary: Former CEO of A.P. State Wakf Board challenged pending disciplinary proceedings against him for allegedly misusing his office to facilitate unauthorized alienation of Wakf land by a caretaker body (Jamat-e-Islami Social Service) that had no authority to sell the property.
litigation_cases.outcome_status: High Court upheld the disciplinary proceedings as validly initiated before the petitioner's retirement and directed their completion within four months; provisional pension continues meanwhile.

litigation_cases.case_name: Madrasa Ahle Sunnath Bahrul Uloon vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors.
litigation_cases.property_involved: Wakf land dedicated to Dargah Hazrath Syed Ali Ishaq Madina Vali, and land adjacent to Haj House
litigation_cases.location: Devada Village, Visakhapatnam District (compensation land); Haj House, Hyderabad (H.No. 5-9-98)
litigation_cases.dispute_summary: Petitioner challenged a government order transferring Rs. 6.63 crore in compensation (received from alienation of the Dargah's Wakf land) from Visakhapatnam to Hyderabad to fund land acquisition for Haj House parking, alleging diversion of Dargah-specific funds.
litigation_cases.outcome_status: Petition dismissed for lack of standing; court found the funds belonged to the Wakf Board generally (not the Dargah specifically) and their use for Haj facilities was a legitimate welfare purpose.

litigation_cases.case_name: Charminar Educational Society vs State Of Telangana
litigation_cases.property_involved: Agricultural land in Survey Nos. 91 and 92, leased from the Waqf Board to an educational institution
litigation_cases.location: Mamidipally Village, Balapur Mandal, Ranga Reddy District
litigation_cases.dispute_summary: Educational society sought a court direction compelling the (newly reconstituted) Telangana Waqf Board to decide its pending lease renewal application after it had cleared outstanding lease dues per an earlier court order.
litigation_cases.outcome_status: Court directed the Waqf Board to examine the renewal application under the Waqf Properties Lease Rules, 2014 and decide promptly, with the institution's operations to continue uninterrupted meanwhile; petition disposed of without costs.

board_member_disclosure_demand.who: Abul Fateh Syed Bandagi Badesha Quadri, Member, Telangana State Waqf Board
board_member_disclosure_demand.date: First reported ~June 7, 2026 (Deccan Chronicle), further covered June 17, 2026 (Telangana Today)
board_member_disclosure_demand.quote_or_summary: Citing the State government's recent enhancement of registration market values and stamp duties, Bandagi Badesha called on the Telangana State Waqf Board to publish a comprehensive, public list of all leased/rented Waqf properties, and to appoint an independent Commission to assess fair, current market-based rents. He said many Waqf properties worth crores of rupees have allegedly been leased at extremely low, decades-old rents, causing huge financial losses to the Board. He specified the disclosure should include: name and location of property, name/details of the tenant or lessee, duration of the lease agreement, rent currently being paid, current registered market value, prevailing market rent, any arrears owed, and the legal status of occupancy. Quotes: 'Waqf properties are sacred institutions meant to benefit the Muslim community' and income from them is meant for 'the welfare of mosques, madrasas, orphanages, charitable institutions and other social and religious causes.' He argued disclosure cuts both ways: 'if everything has been managed properly, public disclosure will strengthen confidence in the Waqf Board,' while 'if irregularities exist, transparency will help initiate corrective measures.' He separately noted the community has 'a right to know how its properties are being administered.' This followed an earlier (Dec 2022) hardline stance where he urged a campaign to boycott the weddings of Waqf tenants who default on rent or pay far below market rate, calling this a violation of lease rules under the Waqf Act 1995 (as amended 2013).

known_lease_rent_examples.property: Madina Commercial Complex, near Charminar, Hyderabad (built during Nizam era for Hajj/Hejaz pilgrim welfare)
known_lease_rent_examples.rent_or_lease_detail: Over 500 shops; expected/fair annual revenue should exceed Rs 6 crore, but tenants pay outdated nominal rents fixed decades ago, with some defaulting entirely; unpaid arrears have accumulated to roughly Rs 30 crore. Rental disputes remain pending in courts; the Waqf Board has not evicted defaulters or revised rents.

known_lease_rent_examples.property: Commercial property in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, under Rajasthan Waqf Board (tenant since 1989)
known_lease_rent_examples.rent_or_lease_detail: Mutawalli issued notice attempting to raise rent from Rs 7,700/month to Rs 50,000/month, basing the hike on 10% of current market value -- disputed as exceeding the statutory reserve-price formula (2.5% of market value under the Waqf Properties Lease (Amendment) Rules, 2020, Section/Rule 7). Tenant sought legal advice to resist the increase and file for injunction.

known_lease_rent_examples.property: Telangana State Waqf Board aggregate holdings (systemic, not a single property, but with named figures)
known_lease_rent_examples.rent_or_lease_detail: Board holds 77,538.07 acres on paper (officially valued around Rs 5 lakh crore), of which 57,423.91 acres (~75%) are under encroachment (estimated encroached value ~Rs 4 lakh crore). The Board actively controls about 20,110 acres yet collects only about Rs 5 crore in annual rent income across its entire portfolio -- illustrating the scale of nominal/uncollected rents. District breakdown of encroachment includes Medak (23,782 of 23,910 acres), Ranga Reddy (13,480 of 14,785), Adilabad (9,189 of 10,119), Mahbubnagar (7,864 acres), Hyderabad (1,469 of 1,785).

known_lease_rent_examples.property: Manikonda Jagir Village land, Rangareddy district, Telangana (Dargah Hazrat Hussain Shah Wali claim)
known_lease_rent_examples.rent_or_lease_detail: Andhra Pradesh Waqf Board had claimed ownership of 1,654.32 acres valued at more than Rs 50,000 crore; Supreme Court ruled in favour of the state government (land held by state, not Waqf), resolving decades-old litigation and affecting numerous private landowners/institutions built on the disputed land.

known_lease_rent_examples.property: Telangana Waqf Board missing property records (admitted in High Court)
known_lease_rent_examples.rent_or_lease_detail: Board admitted that records for 2,186 Waqf properties are missing entirely, illustrating why individual rent/tenant/mutawalli data is largely undisclosed -- reinforcing the need for a reconstructed transparency layer.

lease_rules.educational_social_pct: 2% per annum of market value (set by 2015 amendment to the Waqf Properties Lease Rules, 2014, Rule 7); a further 2020 amendment reportedly reduced this floor to 1% per annum for hospitals, educational institutions and social-sector use (sources vary/conflict on the exact current post-2020 figure -- treat 1-2% as the illustrative range and cite both amendments)
lease_rules.commercial_pct: 2.5% per annum of market value (set by the 2015 amendment, Rule 7; retained at 2.5% in most 2020-amendment descriptions, though at least one source describes a reduction to 1.5% -- treat 1.5-2.5% as the illustrative range)
lease_rules.approval_thresholds: Waqf Properties Lease Rules, 2014 (notified 3 June 2014) originally set reserve price at a flat 5% of market value; amended 26 August 2015 to split into the 2%/2.5% (social vs commercial) structure above. Rule 17 (long-term leases): a lease exceeding the short-term ceiling and extending up to 30 years may be granted for commercial, education, or health purposes only with State Government approval; originally leases over 1 year needed such approval with a 3-month deemed-approval window, later amended to leases over 3 years needing approval with a 45-day deemed-approval window (i.e., if the State Government does not respond within 45 days, permission is deemed granted). Separately, leases with assessed monthly rental income up to Rs 3,000 (as of 3 June 2014) do not require newspaper advertisement, while any property with assessed rental above Rs 3,000/month must go through competitive/highest-bidder tender. Mutawallis, Waqf Board members/managing-committee members and their close relatives (spouse, parents, children) are barred from bidding on leases of the property they administer. Market value = the value used for registering a conveyance at the Registrar/Sub-Registrar's office (i.e., government-notified guideline/circle-rate value).

existing_welfare_programs.name: Waqf-alal-aulad maintenance support via UMEED Portal (Rule 8(2), Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development (UMEED) Rules, 2025)
existing_welfare_programs.administering_body: Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India, in coordination with respective State/UT Waqf Boards
existing_welfare_programs.scale_or_amount: New (2025) digital module enabling widows, divorced women, and orphans to apply online for maintenance support from family/private ('waqf-alal-aulad') endowment properties, with Aadhaar-based beneficiary authentication and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) of the maintenance amount to bank accounts; specific rupee scale not centrally fixed (varies by property/case)

existing_welfare_programs.name: Central Waqf Council pre-matric and post-matric scholarship/fellowship schemes
existing_welfare_programs.administering_body: Central Waqf Council (statutory body, Ministry of Minority Affairs)
existing_welfare_programs.scale_or_amount: Scholarships for minority students in Classes I-X (minimum 50% marks required; at least 30% of awards reserved for girls); fellowships for M.Phil/Ph.D. students (30% reserved for women); State Waqf Boards additionally receive 50%-matching-share grants from the Central Waqf Council for scholarships to students in Classes IX-XII, technical/ITI diploma courses, and Madrasa (Islamic) education

existing_welfare_programs.name: Manipur Waqf Board one-time financial assistance for widows/destitute women
existing_welfare_programs.scale_or_amount: One-time financial assistance to selected poor/needy widows and destitute women, continuously run since 1996-97; funded via a mandatory 7% contribution of net annual income from all registered Waqfs to the Board, plus state grants and Central Waqf Council matching-share scholarship grants; Board itself describes the assistance as limited/'meager' due to funding constraints

existing_welfare_programs.name: Punjab Waqf Board Pension Policy (widow, disability, old-age, destitute pensions)
existing_welfare_programs.scale_or_amount: Eligibility mirrors the Punjab Government Social Security Department's own pension schemes but restricted to Muslim beneficiaries; amount tracks the state Social Security pension rate (raised from Rs 500/month to Rs 750/month, with further proposed increase to Rs 1,500/month under old-age/widow/disability schemes)

existing_welfare_programs.name: Karnataka State Wakf Foundation for Women Development -- medical assistance and Bidaai/Shaadi Bhagya marriage assistance
existing_welfare_programs.administering_body: Government of Karnataka / Karnataka State Wakf Foundation for Women Development (state minority welfare scheme adjacent to the Wakf ecosystem, covers Muslim, Christian, Jain, Buddhist and Parsi minority women)
existing_welfare_programs.scale_or_amount: Rs 50,000 given per beneficiary at time of marriage to purchase essential household items under the Bidaai/Shaadi scheme; separately, up to Rs 1 lakh financial assistance to Muslim women for major medical treatment (e.g., cancer, heart surgery). Note: scheme has faced funding suspensions in some budget years.

existing_welfare_programs.name: Telangana/undivided Andhra Pradesh Waqf Board mass marriage and orphanage sponsorship
existing_welfare_programs.scale_or_amount: Organizes mass/collective marriages for poor Muslim community members and sponsors orphanages in multiple cities; also runs vocational/technical training for Muslim youth. Specific per-beneficiary rupee figures not published.

waqf_development_corp.role: National Waqf Development Corporation Limited (NAWADCO) is a Government of India-owned Section 25 (not-for-profit) company under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, incorporated 31 December 2013 (established January 2014) following a recommendation of the Sachar Committee report. It provides technical, financial, and legal support to State Waqf Boards and Waqf institutions to redevelop under-utilized Waqf land into income-generating commercial/institutional assets, and also directly undertakes development projects (via partner developers/concessionaires) on Waqf land. Its funding model (using government/taxpayer funds to develop religiously-designated private endowment land) has drawn political criticism, including from Union Minister Smriti Irani, who called it an anomaly among Section 25 companies.
example_projects: Partnership with NBCC (National Buildings Construction Corporation) -- 2015 project-specific MoU to develop four Waqf Board properties as institutional/commercial complexes at an estimated combined cost of Rs 398 crore: Gulistan Shadi Mahal, Masjid-e-Mavalli, and Dargah Hazrat Attaullah Shah (Bangalore, Karnataka) plus Takiya Chand Shah (Jodhpur, Rajasthan)

Earlier-stage NAWADCO/NBCC identification of a larger pipeline: one property in Delhi, two in Rajasthan, six in Madhya Pradesh, and seven in Karnataka earmarked for institutional/commercial redevelopment; two Rajasthan projects specifically advanced -- a hospital in Jodhpur and a school in Ajmer

Feasibility studies/evaluations completed for 10 Waqf properties across Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Haryana, and Rajasthan by NAWADCO-engaged real estate experts, to be forwarded to respective State Governments for redevelopment approval
2023-era Expression of Interest (EoI) invited for development of Waqf properties at Panipat (Haryana) and Jaipur (Rajasthan)
